A second review round (Cursor Bugbot and copilot-pull-request-reviewer, both re-reviewing head 242f39d8b) found the first round's own CWE-78 fix had a correctness gap: git grep -f (and -e given a single argument with an embedded newline) matches per line, not as one block, so a multi-line needle can false-confirm on any one of its lines; reproduced empirically via a Python subprocess argv test ruling out shell reinterpretation, then fixed in 59ba674c5 by scoping git grep to single-line needles (wc -l check) and routing any multi-line or provenance claim through git log -S alone. The same commit fixed a disposition-table conflation and a template field assuming output a refutation never produces. 0e119a109 added a converse-guard test proving every plugin root shipping reviewer-findings on disk is covered by the hand-maintained PLUGIN_ROOTS map, via the canonical check_plugin_frontmatter_self_containment.plugin_roots() helper rather than a raw filesystem walk.

While 59ba674c5/0e119a109 were staged locally (not yet pushed), Cursor Bugbot's Autofix cloud agent pushed 35f56343b directly to this branch: a colliding push from an external automated agent, not a human or this session. It rewrote the same git grep -f fix to git grep -n -F -e "$NEEDLE" and added a second, competing converse-guard test to conftest.py using a raw REPO_ROOT.rglob("skills/reviewer-findings/SKILL.md") walk. Investigated both before reconciling: re-ran the same subprocess reproduction against -e "$NEEDLE" and it still false-confirmed on the needle's second line alone, so -e carries the identical defect as -f; the raw rglob walk descends into the nested checkouts under .claude/worktrees/ that .claude/rules/plugin-self-containment.md documents as a known trap (independently flagged by a fresh Copilot review on the same PR), and it referenced REPO_ROOT, a name that exists only in _helpers.py, so the auto-merged conftest.py would have raised NameError at collection. Reconciled non-destructively per the system prompt's git safety rules (no rebase, amend, or force-push over another party's commits): git merge origin/claude/autoplan-nlvjlh at adb22f494, keeping the empirically-verified -f/wc -l wording in both the Process step and MUST 5, and dropping Bugbot's conftest.py addition entirely in favor of the existing test_every_on_disk_root_shipping_this_skill_is_covered, which already uses the canonical helper and does not walk the filesystem.

The same fresh Copilot pass that caught the .claude/worktrees/ walk also flagged two follow-on gaps in the multi-line fix: <path> in every git grep/git log -S example is drawn from the same untrusted finding as the needle text and was not documented as quoted (CWE-78), and the git log -S guidance made no allowance for a shallow checkout (.github/workflows/claude.yml:47,88 sets fetch-depth: 1). Verified both before fixing: confirmed the fetch-depth setting via grep, then empirically tested git log -S against a depth-1 clone and found it answers a single-commit presence question correctly (git diffs the shallow boundary as a root commit) but cannot answer a claim about when a value changed across commits never fetched, narrower than Copilot's unverified blanket framing. Fixed in e77bace87: named -- <path> explicitly with the same never-splice treatment as the needle, and added a narrow shallow-checkout caveat scoped to what was actually verified, with two new structural tests, both mutation-killed by substituting the exact wording and confirming the assertion fails, then restoring a byte-identical file. Updated the PR description to disclose the extract_session_episode.py production-behavior change (a real gap: the fix in an earlier review-response phase was never mentioned in the PR body's Changes section) and rebound the QA report and this log to the final commit.

Ran the full pre_pr.py in the background before pushing the reconciled branch (per push-lock.md discipline, since it takes minutes). First full run at e77bace87 caught a real, self-inflicted regression the merge introduced: Mypy Changed Files (ratchet) failed on tests/skills/reviewer-findings/conftest.py:35, Returning Any from function declared to return Path. Root cause: conftest.py loads _helpers.py via importlib.util (required under --import-mode=importlib, which never adds a test file's own directory to sys.path), so mypy cannot follow the dynamic import and infers _helpers.PLUGIN_ROOTS as Any; the plugin_root fixture then returns Any from a function declared -> Path. Fixed in a8dd1af60 by annotating the module-level PLUGIN_ROOTS: dict[str, Path] = _helpers.PLUGIN_ROOTS with the same type _helpers.py already declares. Verified narrowly with a direct mypy invocation, then re-ran the full pre_pr.py: Mypy Changed Files now PASS, leaving only Session End Validation failing on this QA report's own staleness (it named conftest.py as code changed after the report's qaCommit), a self-referential gap closed by this commit's rebind to a8dd1af60. A stray check-in message scheduled before this session's git-divergence discovery arrived mid-wait, referencing an already-superseded head (242f39d8b); replied with corrected live state rather than acting on it, per the repository's evidence-over-inference discipline.

A ninth Copilot review round (4 comments) on PR #5178 found the eighth round's own fix was lossy: NEEDLE=$(cat <needle-file>) and PATH_SPEC=$(cat <path-file>) both use plain command substitution, which strips every trailing newline the file has, so a needle ending in blank lines is searched as a shorter string than the finding quoted, and a cited path ending in a newline is silently truncated to a different, possibly pre-existing path (CWE-20). Verified empirically: X=$(cat f) on a file ending in two newlines loses both; X=$(cat f; printf x); X=${X%x} (append a sentinel byte, strip it back off) round-trips the bytes exactly. Fixed by requiring the sentinel idiom at all 4 call sites across reviewer-findings/SKILL.md (3) and pr-comment-responder/references/workflow.md (1). While investigating, found the QA report's existing claim that the redundant [ -s <needle-file> ] check had been dropped in round five did not match the shipped SKILL.md (still present in 3 places, reintroduced accidentally during the round-six CWE-78 rewrite); fixed by removing it, making the report's claim true rather than rewriting the report to describe the wrong reality. New test file tests/skills/reviewer-findings/test_reviewer_findings_trailing_newline_safety.py (kept separate from the 449-line test_reviewer_findings_premise_verification.py to stay under the 500-line taste-count-ratchet ceiling): positive coverage for the needle and path recipes across both plugin roots plus workflow.md, and a negative control proving the check requires the exact sentinel recipe, not any "$(cat" substring (the fix's own warning prose names the bad pattern too). Mutation-killed by reverting each recipe in the shipped files in turn and confirming only the matching test(s) failed, then restoring byte-identical (diff confirmed). Full suite: 457 passed.
